text:
Alice Mendez: morning handoff — quick status. I'm primary for US-west today but I'll be offline 13:00-14:30 PDT for a dentist appt. Morgan, can you cover the gap as primary? :wave:

Morgan Brooks: yep I can take primary for that window. I'll be on mute otherwise but reachable via phone if paged.

Alice Mendez: thanks. leaving my checklist: 1) watch hosted-api error-rate dashboard (link below), 2) ensure canary traffic is pinned to stable model, 3) if error-rate > 5% for 10m escalate.

incident-bot: alert: hosted-api error-rate spike detected (5.8% 5m avg) — see https://dash.redwood/hosted-api/errors :rotating_light:

Raj Patel: seeing the bot. I can validate requests now. Does this impact all regions or just US-west?

Chen Li: tracing looks like a KV cache eviction bug cascading into timeouts. A few 502s from runtime pods in west-1.

Maya Ortiz: customer-impact update: two largest customers in US-west experiencing elevated latencies and some timeouts on batch embedding jobs. CS alerted.

Morgan Brooks: I'm on primary now. I'm going to run the mitigation from the runbook: restart runtime pods incrementally, switch canary to previous stable if restarts don't help.

Alice Mendez: pointer to runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/oncall/runtime-kv-eviction. Do the rolling restarts with 30s pause between pods.

Chen Li: adding logs: here's the short grep I ran: ```bash
kubectl logs -l app=runtime -n prod | grep "kv cache miss" | tail -n 50
``` shows repeated "eviction triggered" messages.

Morgan Brooks: started restart on runtime-57, waiting 45s.

incident-bot: deployment-bot: canary traffic switched to model-stable-v2 by Morgan Brooks.

Raj Patel: if restarts fail, escalation path: page Eng Lead (Alice Mendez) -> Eng Director (Leo Tan) -> SRE Pager (oncall@sre.redwood) -> exec on-call for customer-impacting. We should follow that order.

Maya Ortiz: CS requested an ETA to share with customers. Any quick mitigation ETA?

Morgan Brooks: if restart resolves, < 10m. If rollback required, 30–45m. I'll update.

Chen Li: suggestion: enable extra KV cache retention flag temporarily (config flag: `runtime.kv.retention_ms=900000`) — low-risk toggle. If you want me to apply it, say go.

Alice Mendez: go for the flag, but coordinate with Morgan — apply on a subset first. Also log the change in the incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/1976543210

Morgan Brooks: applying retention flag to runtime-57 now.

incident-bot: config-change: `runtime.kv.retention_ms` updated on pod runtime-57 by Morgan Brooks.

Raj Patel: reminder on paging rules (TL;DR): page primary oncall for SEV-2/SEV-1, page Eng Lead if customer-impacting > 30m or multiple customers affected, page SRE Pager for infra-level outages, page exec on-call only if contractual SLA breach imminent. Use `/page oncall` in slack or the PagerDuty flow.

Alice Mendez: adding a handoff note: Morgan will cover 13:00-14:30 PDT. After that Morgan relays to Chen if still unstable. If any paging occurs during my absence, please follow Raj's escalation order.

Maya Ortiz: CS will keep customers updated: initial message sent, ETA updated to 10m.

Morgan Brooks: runtime-57 looks healthy post-flag, error-rate down to 1.9% 3m avg. I'll continue rolling to two more pods then monitor.

Chen Li: great. I'll prepare a post-incident blameless write-up and capture the KV eviction root cause.

Leo Tan: quick ask: if this becomes a recurring pattern, let's add an automated alert that triggers the retention toggler as a safe fallback. Filing a follow-up ticket.

Alice Mendez: perfect. I'll update the oncall checklist and add the short snippet for the retention flag. Thanks everyone — keep updating here. :pray:

Morgan Brooks: rolling restarts finished. Error-rate steady at 1.7%. Closing the immediate mitigation, will hand back to Alice at 14:30 PDT.

incident-bot: thread closed by Morgan Brooks (resolved) — final severity: SEV-2 (partial customer impact), duration 22m.
